events.what: IPMA's red wind warning for the Lisbon district runs from 12:00 to 21:00 on the third day of Web Summit Lisbon 2026, with orange rain and sea warnings the same day.

Between IPMA's file read at 16:32 UTC and the same file read at 18:32 UTC, the Lisbon rain warning for Wednesday 11 November rises from orange (05:00 to 18:00) to red from 12:00 to 18:00 (orange 05:00 to 12:00). The time of the change is not known.

Between IPMA's file read at 22:32 UTC on 10 November and the same file read at 00:32 UTC, the red rain warning for Wednesday 11 November moves three hours earlier, to 09:00 to 18:00 (orange 00:00 to 09:00). The time of the change is not known.

Between IPMA's file read at 08:32 UTC and the same file read at 10:32 UTC, the wind warning for the Lisbon district is lowered from red (12:00 to 21:00) to orange (09:00 to 21:00); red remains for rain only. The time of the change is not known.

IPMA reissues the Lisbon warnings at 12:34 UTC (seen in the file read at 14:32): red rain now 12:34 to 15:00 with yellow to 18:00, wind orange 12:34 to 18:00 with gusts up to 90 km/h, sea orange 12:34 to 21:00; all lower or shorter than the 09:00 to 21:00 warnings listed before.

IPMA reissues the Lisbon warnings at 15:06 UTC (seen in the file read at 16:32): the red rain warning is gone, replaced by yellow rain until 18:00; wind stays orange (gusts up to 90 km/h) until 18:00 and the sea orange until 21:00. No red warning remains for Lisbon.

IPMA reissues the Lisbon warnings at 15:56 UTC (seen in the file read at 18:32): the wind warning is gone, rain stays yellow until 18:00 and the sea orange until 21:00, the only orange warning left. The file lists no wind warning for Lisbon at that reading (an absence, so no quote).

By the 20:32 UTC readings IPMA has reissued the Lisbon warnings (19:09 UTC) so that only the sea warning remains (orange to 21:00, then yellow to 03:00), and Web Summit's homepage no longer carries the Thursday announcement (it was there at 18:32). The times of the changes are not known.

About 7.30pm UTC on Tuesday Web Summit confirms that Wednesday's events are cancelled, after the Portuguese prime minister's recommendation (an hour earlier) and the mayor of Lisbon's remark that 'everything indicates' it could not function; Portugal is under a state of alert. Source: The Irish Times, not Web Summit's own pages.
Shortly after 11.30am UTC on Wednesday Web Summit emails ticket holders 'Web Summit is back tomorrow'. Source: The Irish Times.
By IPMA's file read at 22:32 UTC the orange sea warning has ended: the only warning left for the Lisbon district is yellow for the sea, 21:00 to 03:00 on 12 November.
IPMA reissues the Lisbon district warnings at 06:35 UTC on 12 November: all are green, to 15 November, including wind. Read from IPMA's file at 10:32 UTC.
